walkthroughs.body_html: Adopted Sendai Japan 2015. 7 global targets to 2030 include reducing global disaster mortality, affected people, economic losses (relative to GDP). 187 countries report progress. ODA for DRR reached $4.9 billion in 2020 (still <0.5 percent of total ODA).

Japan tsunami warning operational since 1952; broadcast within 3 minutes of detection. Saved many lives in 2011 despite massive surge. Bangladesh cyclone warning + 12000 shelters reduced Cyclone Bhola (1970) 500000 deaths to Cyclone Sidr (2007) 3400 deaths.

Chile updated codes after 1985 quake; survived 2010 Mw 8.8 with 525 deaths vs Haiti's 220000 from Mw 7.0. Japan's seismic isolation in Tokyo Sky Tree (634 m) damps shaking. California Field Act (1933) requires school seismic design. Codes only work if enforced.

mcqs.q: Sendai Framework runs to which year?
What is the difference between a natural hazard and a natural disaster?
options: They are the same thing — any earthquake or hurricane is a disaster.
Burgess is for American cities and Hoyt is for European cities.
A natural hazard is a physical event with potential to cause harm; it becomes a disaster only when it affects vulnerable people and causes significant impact.
A hazard happens on land and a disaster happens at sea.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the Burgess and Hoyt urban land use models?
options: Burgess (1925) describes concentric rings radiating from the CBD; Hoyt (1939) describes sectors (wedges) extending along transport routes — recognising how transport shapes urban growth.
Burgess is for American cities and Hoyt is for European cities.
A hazard happens on land and a disaster happens at sea.
Burgess and Hoyt models show the same thing in different drawings.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes typically cause more deaths in LICs than HICs?
options: LICs have more earthquake deaths because more earthquakes happen there.
A hazard happens on land and a disaster happens at sea.
LICs often have poorly enforced building codes, weak emergency response, dense informal housing and limited preparedness — not because the earthquakes are stronger.
HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.
